page.layout: One printed page of text in a single column; at the right edge a partial facing page with cut-off marginal fragments (not transcribed). Page number and running head at the top.

main_text.p: De actis Apostolorum liber est qui historiam à Luca conscriptam de Apostolorum ministerio, doctrina, gestisq; omnibus ad perfectum doctrinæ & ecclesiasticæ gubernationis exemplar sufficientem continet. Ex inscriptione. ex 2. Tim 3 10.11.12. 14.15

Apocalypsis est liber à Iohanne Apostolo & κατ' ἐξοχὴν Theologo dicto, conscriptus, qui prophetia de ijs quæ ipsius seculo, & per omnia secula, præcipuè sub Antichristo ecclesiæ eventura sint, iuxta Christi ipsius apocalypsin continet. cap.1.cap.vlt.

Dogmatici libri sunt epistolæ ab Apostolis conscriptæ, vt doctrinam suam totam, ex ecclesiarum suarum circumstantijs omnibus ecclesiæ necessitatibus applicatam, perfectè literis proprijs consignatam relinquerent. Ioa.17.17.20. Eph.3.20.Apo.21. 14. Rom. 19.16.17.1.Cor.11.cap.14.cap.16. Eph.3.1.2. 3. Gal.6. 15.Col.4.16. 1.Thess. 5. 26. 1.Tim. 3.17. & 5.13.14. Tit.1.5.Heb. 6,3. 2. Pet.3. 1. Iudæ. 1.5. Ioh, 1.1. 1. Pet.5.12.
Epistolæ sunt Particulares. Ex ordine & inscriptionibus Epist.Pauli & aliorum. Catholicæ.
Particulares sunt quæ particularibus personis scriptæ fuerunt.
Sunt Ecclesijs particularibus, aut Personis particularibus.
Ecclesijs particularibus scriptæ sunt à Paulo nouem: ad Romanos vna, ad Corinth. duæ, ad Galat. vna, ad Ephes. vna, Philip. vna, Coloss. vna, Thess. duæ.

page.notes: Marginal fragments on the right facing page are cut off and not transcribed. Greek in the Apocalypsis paragraph is rendered approximately; the bracketed Epistolæ diagram is given as a running sentence where its braces could not be fully resolved. "Philip." is partly illegible in the scan.
